---
title: "Multilingual Stringology Bibliography & Terminology Rosetta Stone"
subtitle: "Primary Academic Papers & Monographs [EN], Chinese IOI National Team Theses (国家集训队论文, [ZH]), Japanese Competitive Programming Treatises [JA], and the 84-Entry Trilingual Rosetta Stone Mapped to Ch 01–Ch 30"
---

Modern competitive programming stringology draws from three deeply interconnected traditions:

- **`[EN]` Theoretical Stringology & Combinatorics on Words**: Established the foundational algebraic and structural theorems of words—Fine–Wilf periodicity (`1965`), Chen–Fox–Lyndon factorization (`1958`) and Duval's linear algorithm (`1983`), Suffix Automata and Compact DAWGs (Blumer et al. `1985–1987`, Crochemore–Rytter `1994–2002`), Palindromic Trees / Eertrees (Rubinchik–Shur `2015–2018`), the **Significant Suffixes Theorem** and **Basic Substring Dictionary / Internal Pattern Matching** (Kociumaka, Radoszewski, Rytter, Waleń `2014–2024`), the **Runs Theorem** (Kolpakov–Kucherov `1999`, Bannai et al. `2017`), **Locally Consistent Parsing & Recompression SLPs** (Cole–Vishkin `1986`, Mehlhorn–Sundar–Uhrig `1997`, Jeż `2015–2016`), **String Attractors & $\tau$-Synchronizing Sets** (Kempa–Prezza `2018`, Kempa–Kociumaka `2019`), **Goulden–Jackson Cluster Generating Functions** (`1979`), and **Tiskin's Seaweed Matrices** (`2008–2015`).
- **`[ZH]` Chinese Olympiad (`NOI` / `WC` / `CTSC` / `国家集训队论文`, 2004–2024)**: Pioneered the competitive programming synthesis of word combinatorics with advanced data structures—most notably **SAM + Persistent Segment Tree Merging on $\operatorname{endpos}$** (`[NOI2018] 你的名字`), **Dynamic SAM + Link-Cut Tree `access` Color-Chain Sweeping** (`陈立杰 2012`, `张天扬 2015`), **3-Case Trie-BFS Generalized SAM** (`刘研绎 2015`), **PAM & Range Distinct Palindrome `slink` Telescoping** (`徐毅 2014`), **Border AP Modulo Shortest Path** (`[WC2016] 论战捆竹竿`, `翁文涛 / 钟知闲 2017`), **Fibonacci Singular Words** (`周任飞 2017`), **Significant Suffixes, Lyndon Trees & Runs 2D Sweep-Lines** (`金策 2019`), **Internal Pattern Matching** (`王修涵 2020`), and **Unit-Monge Seaweed Matrices** (`潘佳奇 / 戴江齐 2021`).
- **`[JA]` Japanese `AtCoder` (`AGC` / `ARC`) & `Kyopro` Ecosystem**: Standardized algebraic and unamortized string formulations—including **$O(\sigma)$ Matrix-Free Invertible Subsequence Automaton Queries** (`maspypy`), **Trace-Zero $\det = -1$ Involution Matrices in $GL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ & Stack-Trie Path LCE** (`noshi91`, `snuke`), **1-FFT / 3-in-2 Wildcard Convolutions** (`Nyaan`), **4-Way Double-Ended Deque PAM** (`tatyam`), and **$O(N)$ Double-Order Lyndon-Root Runs Enumeration** (`henkoku`, `noshi91`).

## 1. Academic Stringology & Combinatorics on Words Canon (`[EN]`)

### 1.1 Foundational Monographs & Textbooks

1. **`[Lothaire83]` / `[Lothaire97]` — M. Lothaire (1983; 1997).** *Combinatorics on Words*. Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications, Vol. 17 (2nd ed., Cambridge University Press).
   - **Core Scope**: Free monoids $\Sigma^*$, primitive and conjugate words ($uv \sim_{\text{conj}} vu$), the **Defect Theorem**, **Fine and Wilf's Periodicity Theorem**, the **Chen–Fox–Lyndon Factorization Theorem**, and the **Critical Factorization Theorem** (Césari–Vincent–Duval).
   - **Textbook Mapping**: [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd).

2. **`[Lothaire02]` — M. Lothaire (2002).** *Algebraic Combinatorics on Words*. Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications, Vol. 90, Cambridge University Press.
   - **Core Scope**: Definitive treatment of **Sturmian words** (Ch. 2, by Jean Berstel & Patrice Séébold: 6-way equivalence of subword complexity $p(n) = n+1$, 1-balancedness, mechanical rotation words $s_{\alpha,\rho}$, and central Sturmian words), episturmian words, and Plandowski's theory of word equations (Ch. 9, by Christian Choffrut & Juhani Karhumäki).
   - **Textbook Mapping**: [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 26`](chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd), [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd).

3. **`[Lothaire05]` — M. Lothaire (2005).** *Applied Combinatorics on Words*. Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications, Vol. 105, Cambridge University Press.
   - **Core Scope**: Algorithmic word combinatorics, suffix automata, Lempel–Ziv factorizations, and autocorrelation analysis of pattern occurrences and waiting times in random strings.
   - **Textbook Mapping**: [`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd), [`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)–[`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd).

4. **`[CR94]` / `[CR02]` — Maxime Crochemore & Wojciech Rytter (1994; 2002).** *Text Algorithms* (Oxford University Press, 1994) & *Jewels of Stringology: Text Algorithms* (World Scientific, 2002).
   - **Core Scope**: Canonical exposition of the **Weak Periodicity Lemma**, dyadic $O(\log N)$ border arithmetic progressions, the **Three-Squares Lemma**, Duval's Lyndon factorization, Suffix Automata (`SAM`), Compact DAWGs (`CDAWG`), Two-Way $O(1)$-space matching, and Rytter's **Singular Words** decomposition of Fibonacci strings.
   - **Textbook Mapping**: [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)–[`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd), [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd).

5. **`[Gusfield97]` — Dan Gusfield (1997).** *Algorithms on Strings, Trees, and Sequences: Computer Science and Computational Biology*. Cambridge University Press.
   - **Core Scope**: Suffix trees (Weiner, McCreight, Ukkonen), $O(1)$ RMQ-LCA Longest Common Extensions ($\operatorname{LCE}$), Landau–Vishkin $k$-mismatch Kangaroo jumps and diagonal wavefronts, and generalized suffix structures.
   - **Textbook Mapping**: [`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 13`](chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd), [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd), [`Ch 19`](chapters/ch19-kmismatch-wavefront-period-dichotomy.qmd).

6. **`[FS09]` / `[GKP94]` — Philippe Flajolet & Robert Sedgewick (2009), *Analytic Combinatorics* (Cambridge University Press, Ch. I.4 & III.7); Ronald L. Graham, Donald E. Knuth, & Oren Patashnik (1994), *Concrete Mathematics* (2nd ed., §8.4).**
   - **Core Scope**: Symbolic language equations for pattern avoidance, autocorrelation polynomials $C_{P,P}(z)$, bivariate cluster generating functions, and **Conway's Penney-Ante / Casino Betting Martingale** ($\mathbb{E}[T_S] = \sum_{k \in \operatorname{Borders}(S)} \sigma^k$).
   - **Textbook Mapping**: [`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)–[`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd).

### 1.2 Periodicity, Border Theory, Lyndon Words & The Runs Theorem (`Parts I–II`, `Ch 01`–`Ch 08`)

7. **`[FW65]` — Nathan J. Fine & Herbert S. Wilf (1965).** *"Uniqueness theorems for periodic functions"*, *Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society*, 16(1), 109–114.
   - **Core Theorem**: If $S$ has periods $p, q$ and length $|S| \ge p + q - \gcd(p, q)$, then $\gcd(p, q) \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$; at $|S| = p + q - \gcd(p, q) - 1$, $\gcd(p, q)$ fails uniquely on central Sturmian words, and below threshold there are $p + q - |S|$ independent character orbits ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 26`](chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd), [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd)).

8. **`[CMR99]` — Maria Gabriella Castelli, Filippo Mignosi, & Antonio Restivo (1999).** *"Fine and Wilf's theorem for three periods and a generalization of Sturmian words"*, *Theoretical Computer Science*, 218(1), 83–94.
   - **Core Theorem**: Characterizes the exact three-period threshold $f(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ via a three-way Euclidean step and introduces episturmian words as the extremal counterexamples ([`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd), [`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd)).

9. **`[Lyndon54]` — Roger C. Lyndon (1954).** *"On Burnside's problem"*, *Transactions of the American Mathematical Society*, 77(2), 202–215.
   - **Core Theorem**: Introduces standard lexicographical words (**Lyndon words** $w \in \mathcal{L}$), defined as primitive words strictly smaller than all of their nontrivial cyclic shifts (equivalently, $\forall v \sqsubset_{\text{suf}} w,\, w \prec_{\text{lex}} v$, [`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)).

10. **`[CFL58]` — Kuo-Tsai Chen, Ralph H. Fox, & Roger C. Lyndon (1958).** *"Free differential calculus, IV. The quotient groups of the lower central series"*, *Annals of Mathematics*, 68(1), 81–95.
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves the **Chen–Fox–Lyndon (CFL) Theorem**: every $S \in \Sigma^+$ admits a unique factorization $S = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_k$ ($w_i \in \mathcal{L}$, $w_1 \ge_{\text{lex}} \cdots \ge_{\text{lex}} w_k$), where $w_k$ is the smallest nonempty suffix of $S$, and establishes the standard factorization $w = uv$ ([`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)).

11. **`[FM78]` / `[FK86]` — Harold Fredricksen & James Maiorana (1978), *"Necklaces of beads in $k$ colors and $k$-ary de Bruijn sequences"*, *Discrete Mathematics*, 23(3), 207–210; Harold Fredricksen & Irving Kessler (1986), *Discrete Mathematics*, 61, 181–188.**
    - **Core Theorem**: The **FKM Algorithm**—concatenating all Lyndon words of length dividing $n$ in lexicographical order generates the lexicographically smallest $k$-ary De Bruijn sequence in $O(1)$ amortized time per symbol ([`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd), [`Ch 28`](chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd)).

12. **`[Duval83]` / `[Duval88]` — Jean-Pierre Duval (1983; 1988).** *"Factorizing words over an ordered alphabet"*, *Journal of Algorithms*, 4(4), 363–381; *"Génération d'une section des classes de conjugaison..."*, *Theoretical Computer Science*, 60(3), 255–283.
    - **Core Theorem**: Computes $\operatorname{CFL}(S)$ in $< 2N$ comparisons and $O(1)$ space via a 3-pointer pre-Lyndon invariant $S[i..k-1] = w^d w'$, yielding $O(N)$ Smallest Cyclic Shift (`最小表示法`) and next-Lyndon word stepping ([`Ch 05`](chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)).

13. **`[KRRW14]` — Tomasz Kociumaka, Jakub Radoszewski, Wojciech Rytter, & Tomasz Waleń (2014 / 2016).** *"Maximum motif and minimal suffix queries in a text"* / *"Minimal Suffixes and Lyndon Words in Substrings"*, *CPM 2014* / *Theoretical Computer Science*.
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves the **Significant Suffixes (`显著后缀`) Theorem**: if suffixes $u, v$ of $S[l..r]$ satisfy $|u| < |v| < 2|u|$ and $u \sqsubset v$, then $u = w u'$ and $v = w^2 u'$ force $\min(u'T, vT) < uT < \max(u'T, vT)$ for every $T \in \Sigma^*$, bounding $|\operatorname{Cand}_{\min}(S[l..r])| \le \lfloor\log_2(r-l+1)\rfloor + 1$ ([`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd)).

14. **`[Barcelo90]` / `[HR03]` — Hélène Barcelo (1990), *"On the action of the symmetric group on the free Lie algebra"*, *JCTA* 55, 93–129; Christophe Hohlweg & Christophe Reutenauer (2003), *"Lyndon words, permutations and trees"*, *Discrete Mathematics* 260, 153–158.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Establishes the structural isomorphism between the **Lyndon Tree** of $\$S$ (built by recursive standard factorization $w = uv$) and the **Min-Cartesian Tree** of $\operatorname{rk}[2..N+1]$ ([`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)).

15. **`[FIRS16]` / `[Bille20]` — Frantisek Franek, A. S. M. Sohidull Islam, M. Sohel Rahman, & William F. Smyth (2016), *"Algorithms to compute the Lyndon Array"*, *Stringology 2016*, 172–184; Philip Bille et al. (2020), *CPM 2020*.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves the Next-Smaller-Suffix identity $i + \lambda[i] = \operatorname{nsv}_{\operatorname{rk}}[i]$ for the Lyndon array, enabling $O(N)$ monotonic-stack construction over $\operatorname{rk}_<$ and $\operatorname{rk}_>$ ([`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)).

16. **`[CR95]` / `[FS98]` / `[BL22]` — Maxime Crochemore & Wojciech Rytter (1995), *"Squares, cubes, and time-space efficient string searching"*, *Algorithmica*, 13(5), 405–425; Aviezri S. Fraenkel & Jamie Simpson (1998), *JCTA* 82, 112–120; Srećko Brlek & Shuo Li (2022).**
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves the **Three-Squares Lemma** ($u^2 \sqsubset v^2 \sqsubset w^2$ with $u$ primitive $\implies |w| \ge |u| + |v|$), implying at most $2$ distinct squares have their rightmost occurrence starting at index $i$ and bounding distinct squares by $\le 2N - 2$ (sharpened to $< N$ by Brlek–Li, [`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)).

17. **`[KK99]` — Roman Kolpakov & Gregory Kucherov (1999).** *"Finding maximal repetitions in a word in linear time"*, *Proceedings of FOCS 1999*, 596–604.
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves $|\mathcal{R}(S)| = O(N)$ and $\sum_{R \in \mathcal{R}(S)} e(R) = O(N)$, and gives the first $O(N)$ Runs enumeration algorithm ([`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)).

18. **`[Bannai17]` — Hideo Bannai, Tomohiro I, Shunsuke Inenaga, Yuto Nakashima, Masayuki Takeda, & Kohei Tsuruta (2015 / 2017).** *"The 'Runs' Theorem"*, *SODA 2015*, 324–332 / *SIAM Journal on Computing*, 46(5), 1501–1514.
    - **Core Theorem**: Resolves the Runs Conjecture ($|\mathcal{R}(S)| \le N - 1 < N$ and $\sum_{R \in \mathcal{R}(S)} e(R) < 3N$) by assigning each run $R = (l, r, p)$ a unique interior Lyndon root $i \in [l+1, l+p]$ under mismatch order $S[r+1] <_R S[r+1-p]$, yielding $O(N)$ Lyndon-array + LCE Runs enumeration ([`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)).

### 1.3 Suffix Structures, `SA-IS`, Internal Pattern Matching & Palindromic Automata (`Parts III–IV`, `Ch 09`–`Ch 17`)

19. **`[Weiner73]` / `[McCreight76]` / `[Ukkonen95]` — Peter Weiner (1973), *SWAT (FOCS) 1973*, 1–11; Edward M. McCreight (1976), *JACM* 23(2), 262–272; Esko Ukkonen (1995), *Algorithmica* 14(3), 249–260.**
    - **Core Theorem**: The classic triad of $O(N)$ suffix tree constructions; Weiner's right-to-left suffix links correspond directly to the Link Tree transitions of $\operatorname{SAM}(S^R)$ ([`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)).

20. **`[Blumer85]` — Anselm Blumer, J. Blumer, David Haussler, Andrzej Ehrenfeucht, M. T. Chen, & Joel Seiferas (1985).** *"The smallest automaton recognizing the subwords of a text"*, *Theoretical Computer Science*, 40, 31–55.
    - **Core Theorem**: Establishes the **Suffix Automaton (`SAM` / `DAWG`)** state bound $|V| \le 2N - 1$, transition bound $|E| \le 3N - 4$, laminar $\operatorname{endpos}$ hierarchy, and exact reversal duality $\mathcal{T}_{\text{link}}(\operatorname{SAM}(S)) \cong \mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S^R)$ ([`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)–[`Ch 11`](chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd)).

21. **`[Blumer87]` / `[Inenaga05]` / `[Stoye00]` / `[Maass00]` — Anselm Blumer et al. (1987), *JACM* 34(3), 578–595; Shunsuke Inenaga et al. (2001 / 2005), *Discrete Applied Math.* 146(2), 156–179; Jens Stoye (2000) & Moritz G. Maaß (2000), *CPM 2000*.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Formalizes the **Compact DAWG (`CDAWG`)** (contracting unary SAM states into maximal repeats $\overleftrightarrow{w}$) and the bi-directional **Symmetric Compact DAWG (`SCDAWG`)** via two-sided closure commutativity $\operatorname{cl}_L(\operatorname{cl}_R(u)) = \operatorname{cl}_R(\operatorname{cl}_L(u))$ ([`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)).

22. **`[DS87]` — Paul F. Dietz & Daniel D. Sleator (1987).** *"Two algorithms for maintaining order in a list"*, *Proceedings of STOC 1987*, 365–372.
    - **Core Theorem**: Provides the $O(1)$ dynamic order-maintenance tag invariant (realized via Scapegoat BSTs with 64-bit interval tags $[L_u, R_u]$) powering hash-free **Suffix Balanced Trees (`后缀平衡树`)** ([`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)).

23. **`[Kasai01]` / `[AKO04]` — Toru Kasai, Gunho Lee, Hiroki Arimura, Setsuo Arikawa, & Kunsoo Park (2001), *CPM 2001*, LNCS 2089, 181–192; Mohamed Ibrahim Abouelhoda, Stefan Kurtz, & Enno Ohlebusch (2004), *J. Discrete Algorithms*, 2(1), 53–86.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves Kasai's $h[\operatorname{rk}[i]] \ge h[\operatorname{rk}[i-1]] - 1$ for $O(N)$ LCP construction and the Three-Way Isomorphism between internal nodes of $\mathcal{T}_{\text{ST}}(S)$ and the **Min-Cartesian Tree** of $\operatorname{height}[2..N]$ ([`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)–[`Ch 13`](chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd)).

24. **`[NZC09]` / `[Fischer11]` — Ge Nong, Sen Zhang, & Wai Hong Chan (2009 / 2011), *"Two efficient algorithms for linear time suffix array construction"*, *DCC 2009* / *IEEE Trans. Computers* 60(10), 1471–1484; Johannes Fischer (2011), *"Inducing the LCP-Array"*, *WADS 2011*, LNCS 6844, 374–385.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Introduces **SA-IS ($L/S$ and LMS Induced Sorting)** in $O(N)$ time via prefix-free LMS substrings and 3-pass bucket inducing, and augments the inducing passes to compute `height` (LCP) simultaneously in $O(N)$ time ([`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)).

25. **`[Kociumaka15]` / `[Kociumaka18]` / `[KRRW24]` — Tomasz Kociumaka, Jakub Radoszewski, Wojciech Rytter, & Tomasz Waleń (2015 / 2024), *"Internal Pattern Matching Queries in a Text and Applications"*, *SODA 2015*, 532–551 / *SIAM J. Comput.*, 53(5), 2024; Tomasz Kociumaka (2018), *PhD Dissertation, University of Warsaw*.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Establishes the **Basic Substring Dictionary (`BSD`)** and **Bounded-Ratio Internal Pattern Matching (`IPM`)** theorem: when $|V| < 2|U|$, $\operatorname{Occ}(U, V)$ forms a single arithmetic progression of step $\operatorname{per}(U)$, enabling $O(\log N)$ internal border queries, $O(1)$ internal period queries, and $O(1)$ substring rank/concatenation comparisons ([`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd)).

26. **`[DJP01]` / `[GJWZ09]` / `[FGKK14]` — Xavier Droubay, Jacques Justin, & Giuseppe Pirillo (2001), *TCS* 255, 539–553; Amy Glen et al. (2009), *EJC* 30(2), 510–531; Gabriele Fici, Travis Gagie, Juha Kärkkäinen, & Dominik Kempa (2014), *"A subquadratic algorithm for minimum palindromic factorization"*, *J. Discrete Algorithms*, 28, 41–48.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Proves the **Droubay–Pirillo $N+1$ Rich Word Bound** ($|\operatorname{Pal}(S)| \le |S| + 1$) and the **Shift-Overlap Invariant** accelerating palindromic factorization DP to $O(N \log N)$ via `slink` AP chains ([`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd)).

27. **`[RS15]` / `[RS17]` / `[RS18]` / `[BKRS17]` — Mikhail Rubinchik & Arseny M. Shur (2015 / 2017 / 2018), *"EERTREE: An efficient data structure for processing palindromes in strings"*, *European J. Combinatorics*, 68, 249–265 (`arXiv:1506.04862`) & *"Counting palindromes in substrings"*, *SPIRE 2017*; Kirill Borozdin et al. (2017), *CPM 2017*.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Formalizes the dual-root **Palindromic Tree (`PAM` / `Eertree`)**, unamortized $O(1)$ direct fail links (`quick_link[u][c]`), **4-Way Deque PAM**, and **Range Distinct Palindrome Queries** via `slink` periodic occurrence telescoping ([`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd)).

### 1.4 Algebraic/FFT Matching, Isomorphism, Grammar SLPs, Subsequences, Seaweed & Words (`Parts V–VII`, `Ch 18`–`Ch 30`)

28. **`[FP74]` / `[Abrahamson87]` / `[Kalai02]` / `[CC07]` — Michael J. Fischer & Michael S. Paterson (1974), *SIAM-AMS Proc.* 7, 113–125; Karl Abrahamson (1987), *SICOMP* 16(6), 1039–1051; Adam Kalai (2002), *SODA 2002*, 655–656; Peter Clifford & Raphaël Clifford (2007), *"Simple deterministic wildcard matching"*, *Information Processing Letters*, 101(2), 53–54.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Reduces wildcard and generalized string matching to **1–3 NTTs** via squared-difference polynomials $\sum P_j T_{i+j}(P_j - T_{i+j})^2 = 0$, Kalai randomized projections, and $\sqrt{M\log M}$ heavy–light bucket splitting ([`Ch 18`](chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd)).

29. **`[LV86]` / `[LV89]` / `[ALP04]` / `[CFPSS16]` / `[GU18]` — Gad M. Landau & Uzi Vishkin (1986; 1989), *TCS* 43 & *J. Algorithms* 10(2); Amihood Amir, Moshe Lewenstein, & Ely Porat (2004), *J. Algorithms* 50(2); Raphaël Clifford et al. (2016), *SODA 2016*; Paweł Gawrychowski & Przemysław Uznański (2018), *"Towards unified approximate pattern matching for Hamming and $L_1$ distance"*, *ICALP 2018*.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Establishes $O(Nk)$ LCE **Kangaroo Jumping**, $O(N + k^2)$ diagonal **Edit-Distance Wavefronts**, and the **$O(N\sqrt{k\log k})$ $2k$-Period Dichotomy** for $k$-mismatch ([`Ch 19`](chapters/ch19-kmismatch-wavefront-period-dichotomy.qmd)).

30. **`[Baker93]` / `[KRRW13]` / `[PALP19]` / `[BCFL10]` / `[Barton16]` — Brenda S. Baker (1993 / 1996), *JCSS* 52(1); Marcin Kubica et al. (2013), *IPL* 113(12); Sung Gwan Park et al. (2019), *"Cartesian tree matching and indexing"*, *CPM 2019* / *TCS* 812; Péter Burcsi et al. (2010), *FUN 2010*; Carl Barton, Tomasz Kociumaka, Chang Liu, Solon P. Pissis, & Jakub Radoszewski (2016 / 2020), *"Indexing weighted sequences"*, *STACS 2016* / *Algorithmica*.**
    - **Core Theorem**: Unifies **Window-Clipped Structural KMP** (`p-KMP`, `Order-KMP`, parent-distance `Cartesian-KMP`), Baker's single-mutation `p-SA`, binary Abelian Parikh continuity $[m_\ell, M_\ell]$, and Barton et al.'s **$1/z$ Heavy-String Decomposition** into $\le \lfloor z \rfloor$ deterministic strings of total length $O(Nz)$ ([`Ch 20`](chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd)).

31. **`[CV86]` / `[MSU97]` / `[Jez15]` / `[Jez16]` — Richard Cole & Uzi Vishkin (1986), *Info. Control* 70; Kurt Mehlhorn, R. Sundar, & Christian Uhrig (1997), *Algorithmica* 17(2); Artur Jeż (2015; 2016), *"Faster fully compressed pattern matching by recompression"*, *ACM TALG* 11(3) & *"Recompression: A simple and powerful technique for word equations"*, *JACM* 63(1).**
    - **Core Theorem**: Alternating RLE (`RComp`) + Cole–Vishkin 6-coloring / **Jeż Recompression** (`PComp`) builds $O(\log N)$-depth SLPs supporting $O(\log N)$ dynamic split/concat/reverse/LCE and $N \le 10^{18}$ word equations ([`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd), [`Ch 26`](chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd)).

### 2.2 Detailed Technical Breakdown of Landmark `国家集训队论文` & Proposition Reports

1. **Chen Lijie (`[ZH-Chen12]`, 2012 & 2014) — SAM Link-Tree Topology, LCT Coupling & Suffix Balanced Trees**:
   - Establishes the $\operatorname{endpos}(u)$ laminar tree invariant where state $u$ covers all suffixes of its longest word of lengths in $[\operatorname{len}(\operatorname{link}(u))+1, \operatorname{len}(u)]$.
   - Couples online SAM construction with a **Link-Cut Tree (`LCT`)** supporting path-add subtree occurrence increments (`[BZOJ 2555]`), and introduces weight-balanced Scapegoat **Suffix Balanced Trees (`后缀平衡树`)** with 64-bit interval tags $[L_u, R_u]$ for $O(\log N)$ online front-prepend suffix sorting ([`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 11`](chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd), [`Ch 14`](chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)).

2. **Xu Yi (`[ZH-Xu14]`, 2014) — Palindromic Automata (`PAM`), Deque PAM & Range Distinct Palindromes (`LOJ #6071`)**:
   - Independently develops the dual-root Palindromic Automaton (`len = -1, 0`), half-length pointers `trans[u]` (`[SHOI2011] 双倍回文`), and 2-ended Deque PAM.
   - Proves the **Periodic Suffix Telescoping Theorem**: along any `slink` chain $(u_1, \dots, u_k)$ at right endpoint $r$, periodicity forces $\operatorname{start}_{r-1}(u_j) = \operatorname{start}_r(u_{j-1})$, so all intermediate Fenwick updates cancel and each chain generates a single contiguous interval update $[\text{prev\_r}(\text{top}(u)) - \operatorname{len}[u] + 2,\; r - \operatorname{len}[\text{top}(u)] + 1]$ ([`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)–[`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd)).

3. **Liu Yanyi (`[ZH-Liu15]`, 2015) — Generalized SAM (`广义 SAM`), Zero-Length Clones & 20-Leaf Tree GSAM**:
   - Proves that naive Trie-DFS insertion into a GSAM degrades to $\Theta(V^2)$ time on $\{\texttt{a}^k\texttt{b} : 1 \le k \le m\}$ and creates unreachable zero-length clones (`len[u] == len[link[u]]`) when `ch[last][c]` already exists (`BP-09`).
   - Establishes the **3-Case Online GSAM Rule**, proves that **Offline Trie-BFS GSAM** runs in strict $O(V\sigma)$ time, and shows that rooting an unrooted tree with $L \le 20$ leaves at every leaf covers all $O(N^2)$ simple paths in $O(LN)$ Trie nodes (`[ZJOI2015] 诸神眷顾的幻想乡`, [`Ch 09`](chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd), [`Ch 29`](chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd)).

4. **Zhang Tianyang (`[ZH-Zhang15]`, 2015–2016) & NOI 2018 Committee — Clipped `endpos` Segment Tree Merging & Dominant Pairs**:
   - Formalizes bottom-up **Persistent Segment Tree Merging on $\operatorname{endpos}$** (`[NOI2018] 你的名字`), proving the exact left-boundary clipping identity $\operatorname{endpos}_S(u) \cap [l + L - 1, r] \neq \emptyset$ and predecessor length-jump $L_{\text{valid}} = \min(L, e_{\max} - l + 1)$ ([`Ch 10`](chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd)).
   - Proves that DSU-on-Tree over a Suffix Tree generates at most **$2N \log_2 N$ Dominant Pairs** $(i^-, i, \ell_u)$ sufficient for 2D range LCP maximization (`CF 1043G`, `CF 1098F`, [`Ch 13`](chapters/ch13-virtual-suffix-trees-dominant-pairs.qmd)).

5. **Weng Wentao & Zhong Zhixian (`[ZH-Weng17]`, 2017) — Border AP Modulo Shortest Path (`[WC2016]`) & `slink` DP**:
   - Proves that grouping $\operatorname{Per}(S)$ into $\le \lceil\log_2 N\rceil$ arithmetic progressions $\{x_k + j \cdot d_k\}$, dynamically switching the shortest-path modulus to $x_k$, and unrolling each $+d_k \pmod{x_k}$ residue cycle from its argmin reduces $O(N^2)$ border knapsack to $O(N \log N)$ time (`[WC2016] 论战捆竹竿`, [`Ch 03`](chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd)).
   - Establishes `slink` shift-overlap DP (`CF 932G`, `CF 906E`) and Shared-Trie Tree PAM ([`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd), [`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)).

6. **Zhou Renfei (`[ZH-Zhou17]`, 2017) — Fibonacci Word Anatomy & Rytter's Singular Words $w_k$**:
   - Proves near-commutativity $F_{k-1}F_{k-2} \leftrightarrow F_{k-2}F_{k-1}$, central palindrome factorization $F_k = \pi_k c_k$ ($|\pi_k| = f_k - 2$), and the infinite **Singular Word Decomposition** $F_\infty = w_0 w_1 w_2 \cdots$, solving $n \le 10^{18}$ prefix distinct-substring, palindrome, and run queries in $O(\log n)$ time via Zeckendorf decomposition ([`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd)).

7. **Jin Ce (`[ZH-Jin19]`, 2019) & Wang Xiuhan (`[ZH-Wang20]`, 2020) — Significant Suffixes, Lyndon Trees, Runs & IPM**:
   - Proves the **Significant Suffixes (`显著后缀`) Theorem** (`[ZJOI2017] 字符串`) and the 1-survivor segment-tree `pushup` theorem ([`Ch 06`](chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd)).
   - Derives the double-order Lyndon array ($\lambda_<, \lambda_>$), proves **Bannai et al.'s Runs Theorem** via interior Lyndon roots, designs the 2D sweep-line + SAM deduplication engine for range square queries (`LOJ #171` / `LOJ #6681`, [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)–[`Ch 08`](chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)), and translates Kociumaka's **Basic Substring Dictionary / IPM** (`[BJWC2018] Border 的四种求法`, [`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd)).

8. **Pan Jiaqi, Dai Jiangqi & Liu Yuchen (`[ZH-Pan21]`, 2021) — Tiskin's Seaweed Matrices & Unit-Monge $\boxdot$**:
   - Proves the anti-Monge permutation cross-difference of semi-local LCS, gives the $O(K\log K)$ monotone-staircase divide-and-conquer for Unit-Monge distance multiplication $\boxdot$, and solves **`[THUPC 2021] 区间 LCS`** and **$O(N\log^2 N)$ Range LIS** ([`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd)).

### 3.2 Detailed Technical Breakdown of the `[JA]` Stringology Canon

1. **`noshi91` (`[JA-noshi91]`) — Runs, Block-Compression SLPs, Non-Abelian $GL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Hashes & Semiring PAM**:
   - *Runs & Lyndon Trees (`Runs の列挙 / Lyndon Array の線形時間構築`)*: Proves why $\operatorname{rk}_>$ must break proper-prefix ties via character inversion $\overline{S}$ rather than $-\operatorname{rk}_<$ (`BP-07`), and seeds all runs in $O(N)$ time from $\lambda_<, \lambda_>$.
   - *Locally Consistent Parsing (`局所一意分割による動的文字列の LCE クエリ`)*: Implements alternating RLE + deterministic Cole–Vishkin 6-coloring to support $O(\log N)$ dynamic split, concat, reverse, and collision-free LCE ([`Ch 21`](chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd)).
   - *Non-Abelian Stack Hashing (`非可換ハッシュによる括弧列・隣接消去判定`)*: Constructs trace-zero $\det = -1$ involution matrices $M_c = \begin{pmatrix} a_c & b_c \\ (1-a_c^2)/b_c & -a_c \end{pmatrix}$ satisfying $M_c^2 = I_2$ for adjacent-equal stack cancellation (`CF 1223F`) and height-indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ generators for directed Dyck strings ([`Ch 29`](chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd)).

2. **`maspy` (`[JA-maspypy]`) — Matrix-Free Invertible Subsequence Algebra & Autocorrelation FPS**:
   - *Invertible Subsequence Matrices (`部分列 DP の行列表示とその逆行列`)*: Proves that the $(\sigma+1)\times(\sigma+1)$ subsequence transition matrix $M_c = I_{\sigma+1} + \mathbf{e}_c\mathbf{1}^\top$ has $\det M_c = 1$ and $O(1)$-sparse inverse $M_c^{-1} = I_{\sigma+1} - \mathbf{e}_c(\mathbf{1}-2\mathbf{e}_c)^\top$. Precomputing $\mathbf{u}_r^\top = \mathbf{e}_{\sigma+1}^\top P_r$ and $\mathbf{v}_{l-1} = P_{l-1}^{-1}\mathbf{1}$ in $O(1)$ per step answers static range distinct subsequence queries on $S[l..r]$ via the dot product $\mathbf{u}_r^\top \cdot \mathbf{v}_{l-1}$ in $O(\sigma)$ time without a segment tree ([`Ch 22`](chapters/ch22-dasg-arch-simon-invertible-matrices.qmd)).
   - *Goulden–Jackson & Automaton DP (`文字列の周期とオートマトン・母関数`)*: Unifies overlap polynomials $C_{i,j}(x)$, Bostan–Mori rational extraction, and Hopcroft-minimized inner-DP DFAs ([`Ch 24`](chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)–[`Ch 25`](chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd)).

3. **`tatyam` (`[JA-tatyam]`), `henkoku` (`[JA-henkoku]`), `Nyaan` (`[JA-Nyaan]`), and `snuke` (`[JA-snuke]`)**:
   - **`tatyam`**: Formalizes 0-Hecke sticky seaweed braids (`Seaweed Matrix による区間 LCS`, [`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd)) and 4-Way Double-Ended Deque PAM (`両端回文木`) with worst-case $O(1)$ lazy surface push-down ([`Ch 16`](chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)).
   - **`henkoku`**: Synthesizes Kociumaka's Basic Substring Dictionary (`内部パターンマッチング (IPM)`), PAM `slink` periodic telescoping (`区間相異なる回文クエリ`), and Parent-Distance Cartesian-Tree KMP ([`Ch 15`](chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd), [`Ch 17`](chapters/ch17-range-palindromes-rich-words.qmd), [`Ch 20`](chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd)).
   - **`Nyaan`**: Provides reference implementations of 1-FFT unit-circle wildcard matching, 3-in-2 complex FFT packing ([`Ch 18`](chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd)), and 64-bit word-parallel Allison–Dix LCS / Myers Edit Distance ([`Ch 23`](chapters/ch23-bit-parallel-lcs-seaweed-matrices.qmd)).
   - **`snuke`**: Establishes $\operatorname{rk}$-descent $L/S$ duality (`AGC 060 D`, [`Ch 12`](chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)), Lyndon tree greedy exchange (`AGC 023 F`, [`Ch 07`](chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)), inverse SA (`ARC 044 D`, [`Ch 27`](chapters/ch27-inverse-reconstruction-inequality-dags.qmd)), De Bruijn BEST counting (`ABC 336 G`, [`Ch 28`](chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd)), and mechanical Sturmian floor sums (`ABC 313 G`, [`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd)).

## 4. Multilingual Stringology Rosetta Stone (`[EN]` $\leftrightarrow$ `[ZH]` $\leftrightarrow$ `[JA]`)

The 84-entry trilingual dictionary below maps every core concept, data structure, combinatorial invariant, and algorithmic reduction across English (`[EN]`), Chinese (`[ZH]`), and Japanese (`[JA]`) to its canonical notation and primary chapter in [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 30`](chapters/ch30-sturmian-singular-thue-morse-morphic-2d.qmd).

| # | English Term (`[EN]`) | Chinese Term (`[ZH]`) | Japanese Term (`[JA]`) | Canonical Notation & Structural Invariant | Primary Chapter |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **01** | Weak / General Period | 周期 / 广义周期 | 周期 (Period) | $p \in \operatorname{Per}(S) \iff S[i] = S[i+p]\; (\forall 1 \le i \le \lvert S\rvert-p)$ | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) |
| **02** | Exact / Full Period (Cyclic Root) | 整周期 / 循环节 | 完全周期 / 最小周期 | $p \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ and $p \mid \lvert S\rvert$ | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) |
| **03** | Proper Border & Period–Border Duality | 真 Border 与周期对偶性 | ボーダーと周期の双対性 | $b \in \operatorname{Border}(S) \iff p = \lvert S\rvert - b \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) |
| **04** | Fine–Wilf Periodicity Theorem | Fine–Wilf 定理 (周期引理) | Fine–Wilf の定理 | $p, q \in \operatorname{Per}(S),\; \lvert S\rvert \ge p + q - \gcd(p, q) \implies \gcd(p, q) \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) |
| **05** | Sub-Threshold Dual-Period Orbits | 亚阈值双周期独立轨道数 | Fine–Wilf 閾値未満の軌道数 | For $\max(p, q) \le N < p + q - \gcd(p, q)$, orbit count is $C(N; p, q) = p + q - N$ | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) |
| **06** | Three-Period Fine–Wilf Theorem | 三周期 Fine–Wilf 定理 | 3周期 Fine–Wilf の定理 | Castelli–Mignosi–Restivo threshold $f(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ (`[CMR99]`) | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd) |

| **08** | Weak Periodicity Lemma | 弱周期引理 | 弱周期性補題 | $p, q \in \operatorname{Per}(S),\; \lvert S\rvert \ge p + q \implies \gcd(p, q) \in \operatorname{Per}(S)$ | [`Ch 01`](chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)–[`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd) |

| **10** | Series Link & Period Difference | 等差数列跳链 (`slink` / `diff`) | 直列リンク (`slink` / `diff`) | $\operatorname{diff}[u] = \operatorname{len}[u] - \operatorname{len}[\operatorname{fail}[u]]$; half-open AP $(\operatorname{slink}[u], u]$ | [`Ch 02`](chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd), [`Ch 04`](chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd) |
